direction_notes: tFUS significantly increased the MRCP source profile amplitude (MSPA) relative to sham ultrasound, and a higher ultrasound pulse repetition frequency (UPRF 3000 Hz) enhanced the MSPA more than a lower UPRF (300 Hz).
safety_notes: No adverse symptoms (headache, neck pain, dental pain, nausea, dizziness, anxiety, abnormal muscle contractions) were reported on questionnaire; however 7 of 15 subjects reported scalp tingling sensation only during the UPRF 3000 Hz session.

exposures.label: tFUS to primary leg motor cortex, UPRF 300 Hz and 3000 Hz

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasound was triggered by the onset of the voluntary foot-pedaling motion signal (detected by an accelerometer) and delivered as a single 500-ms sonication per trial; about 120 trials of right foot pedaling were conducted per session, with subjects initiating pedaling roughly every 3-5 seconds. Two UPRF conditions (300 Hz and 3000 Hz) plus a sham condition were tested in three sessions in random order. In the sham condition the transducer was physically detached from the scalp by 4-6 cm while still transmitting at UPRF 3000 Hz.
